title: Erratum: published soil temperatures still have the wrong deepest depth
description: The deepest soil layer is 2.872 m thick, but that thickness was accidentally used as its centre depth. The real centre is 3.164 m, and layer bounds are missing from the old publication.
example: A user asking for temperature around 3 m can interpolate against the wrong location, or miscalculate soil heat storage. The temperature numbers themselves do not need to be changed for this coordinate repair.
scientific_evidence: Every first-file header across all 138 datasets uses 2.872 m, which is the sixth layer thickness, as its centre. Correct bounds are 1.728–4.6 m; all six depth bounds are absent. The error is 0.292 m in the deepest coordinate.
impact: Depth alignment, interpolation, soil heat-storage calculations and permafrost diagnostics can be biased. This is an axis-value error, so High is more appropriate than a cosmetic metadata classification.
recommended_action: Use the shared CABLE centres [.011,.051,.157,.4385,1.1855,3.164] m and native interfaces, with depth bounds. Preserve temperature values and masks, and verify coordinate alignment with layered mrsol.
development_team_action: MOPPy development: #851 is already merged for #850. Validate current code and document the release containing it. Publication team: replace all 138 current tsl releases. Do not create a duplicate source fix.
extent_statement: Complete file list within the identified release versions; numerical confirmation was sampled, not a scan of every value.
publication_action: No withdrawal, retraction, replacement or ESGF submission performed by this task.
